learning_objective: 🎯 [Kids will learn how to use Adjectives (describing words) to make their sentences more colorful, descriptive, and detailed.]
warm_up_hook: 🎨 Imagine a world without colors or sizes. A 'big, shiny, red apple' would just be an 'apple'. Adjectives are the magic paintbrushes that add color and details to our Nouns!

lesson_modules.teaching_content: An Adjective is a describing word. It tells us more about a noun. It can tell us the color, size, shape, taste, or how someone feels.
Adjectives don't just describe how things look; they can also tell us 'How many?'. Numbers used before nouns act as adjectives!
Adjectives usually sit right IN FRONT of the noun they are describing. Sometimes, they can come after helping verbs like is/am/are.

practice_mcq_quiz.question: ❓ Which word in this sentence is the Adjective? 'The small puppy barked.'
❓ Which Adjective best describes ice cream?

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Circle the adjective and underline the noun it describes: 'I am wearing a blue shirt.'
subjective_practice.hint: What is the naming word? What word tells us the color of that naming word?

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Fill in the blank with a number adjective: 'A triangle has ________ sides.'
subjective_practice.hint: Think of how many sides a slice of pizza has.

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Write the opposite adjectives for: 1. Hot _____  2. Tall _____

activity_or_assignment.title: 👁️ I Spy: Adjective Edition
activity_or_assignment.instructions: Play 'I Spy' with a friend or family member. Instead of just saying the color, use two adjectives! Example: 'I spy with my little eye something that is soft and green!' (A cushion).

chapter_summary: ⭐ Adjectives are describing words that tell us more about nouns.
⭐ They tell us about color, size, shape, taste, feelings, or how many.
⭐ Numbers can also be adjectives when they tell us 'how many'.
⭐ Adjectives usually come just before the noun they describe.
